Heard finally with the consent of learned Counsel for the appellants and respondent Nos. 2 at the admission stage.

2. The appellants, being dissatisfied with the judgment and order dated 09.12.2021, passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal - 2, Nagpur (hereinafter referred to as ' Tribunal), in Claim Petition No. 1096/2015, whereby the claim petition was partly allowed, have preferred this appeal for enhancement of the compensation.

3. The original claimants/appellants, i.e. widow and three major and independent sons, have filed a claim on account of the death of the husband of claimant No.1 and father of claimant Nos. 2 to 4, i.e.
Jawaharlal Nemchand Jain, on 25.05.2015 in a motor vehicle accident when he was riding the Activa bearing registration No. MH-49/C-1701 (hereinafter referred to as 'Activa') was going towards his shop from his home.

On the old Bhandara road near the petrol pump, a truck with registration No. MH-31/CQ-6117 (hereinafter referred to as 'Truck') came in high speed in a rash and negligent manner, and gave a forcible dash to the Activa.
Due to the said dash, the deceased fell on the road and sustained injuries.
So, he was taken to the Rahate Nursing Home, Nagpur, where he died during treatment in the hospital.

Accordingly, on the complaint of the deceased, the offence was registered against the driver of the truck vide Crime No. 197/2015, at Lakadganj police station,
for the offence punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code.

4. At the time of the accident, the deceased Jawaharlal Jain was doing business and was earning an income of Rs. 6,00,000/- per annum from the said business, but due to his death, the claimants have suffered a mental trauma and monetary loss.
5. The respondent No.1 was the owner of the truck, and the said truck was insured with respondent No.2/Insurance Company.
Therefore, both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, the claimants have filed the claim for compensation.
6. Though respondent No.1/owner was served with the summons, he failed to appear before the Tribunal, and therefore, the petition was proceeded ex parte against him vide order dated 09.12.2016.

sentences.text: 2 7. The respondent No.2/Insurance Company filed its written statement and resisted the claim on the ground that the deceased himself was negligent and rash in driving the Activa.
He was not holding an effective driving licence, and therefore, the claimants are not entitled to claim compensation.
The claimants failed to implead the owner and insurer of the Activa; thus, the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Alternatively, it is contended that since the two vehicles were involved in the accident, both drivers should be held responsible for the said accident.
However, it has not been disputed that the truck was insured with it at the time of the accident .
The respondent No.2/Insurance Company specifically pleaded that the claimants failed to produce documents showing that the deceased was a businessman and earning an income.
Similarly, it was averred that the deceased and claimant No.1, i.e., the wife of the deceased, were dependent on the income of the claimant Nos. 2 to 4.

However, it was alternatively contended that at most, Claimant No. 1 could be considered a dependent of the deceased, and Claimants Nos. 2 to 4 were not dependents; therefore, it prayed for the dismissal of the application.
8. After considering the rival pleading of the parties, the learned Tribunal has framed the issues.
Pursuant to the issues, claimants have examined the four witnesses and produced and proved the documents.
On the other hand, respondents did not adduce any evidence in support of their defence.
9. Upon considering the evidence and submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties, the learned Tribunal vide impugned order, partly allowed the claim of the claimants.
Being dissatisfied with the same, the claimants have preferred this appeal.
10. Heard learned Counsel for the appellants and respondent No. 2, Insurance Company.
Despite service of the notice, none appears for respondent No.1.

Perused the impugned judgment, record,
and proceedings as well as the judgments relied on in Seema Rani & Ors. Vs. The Oriental Insurance Company Limited & Ors, 2025 All SCR 1047, and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mrs. Divya Girish Kapadia and Others, 2023(3) T.A.C. 50 (Bom.).
11.

12. It is pertinent to note that during the pendency of the appeal, original claimant No.1, i.e. the widow of the deceased, died on 14.08.2023, and therefore, her name was deleted from the array of the claimants.
Her legal heirs are already on record.

Similarly, the Insurance Company has not preferred any appeal against the impugned judgment and order, which itself indicates that the Insurance Company has no grievance about the impugned judgment and award.

13. Learned Counsel Ms. Rohini Mankar for the appellants vehemently contended that the learned Tribunal has not considered the mandate in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 , and thereby, erred in granting less compensation under the head of consortium.

To buttress his submission, she has relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Seema Rani (supra).
14.
She further argued that in view of the mandate in Mrs. Divya (supra), all the claimants are entitled to get consortium under the head of filial consortium with a 10% increase as above.
The learned Tribunal failed to grant the same.
However, she does not dispute that, in Pranay Sethi (supra), no separate consortium was awarded under the three categories of the consortium.

Hence,
she has urged that the appeal be allowed.
15. Per contra, learned Counsel for the respondent No.2 submitted that the judgment and order passed by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and no interference is required in it.
During the argument, she took me through the evidence of PW.1 and pointed out that claimants Nos. 2 to 4 were residing separately, earning, and maintaining themselves.

Consequently, in light of the mandate in New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Vinish Jain and others (2018) 3 SCC. 61, the major sons have their own source of income and were not dependent on the deceased; therefore,
they do not fall within the purview of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act to claim the compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Vinish Jain and others (2018) 3 SCC. 61
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, they are not entitled to the relief as claimed and urged the dismissal of the appeal.
16. At the outset, the short question that arises is whether the appellants are entitled to claim enhancement of the compensation under the head of filial consortium for the death of their father ."

While considering the said factor, I would like to reproduce the admission given by the claimant No.1, in his cross-examination as under :
"We all are residing separately.
Even all petitioners are residing separately and doing their independent business and maintaining themselves.
At the time of accident my deceased father Jawaharlal was residing with me, but prior to one and half year of his death, we are residing independently.

"
Similarly, he admitted that at the time of the incident, the deceased was 82 years old.
17. The grievance of the claimants is only that the Tribunal failed to grant compensation under the head of filial consortium.
However, neither the appellants nor respondent No.2 has any grievance with the rest of the findings.
They are not disputing the remaining findings.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to deal with the above grievance only.

18. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it appears that the learned Tribunal, according to the mandate in Pranay Sethi (supra), has rightly granted the compensation under all heads, including under the head of consortium.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the learned Tribunal commits any perversity or illegality in that regard.

However, in view of the judgment in Divya Girish Kapadia (supra), Appellant Nos. 2 to 4 claim that they are also entitled to receive the compensation under the head of filial consortium, which the learned Tribunal did not grant.

sentences.text: While dealing with the said issue, it appears that PW.1, i.e. claimant No.2, Shantilal, during his cross-examination has categorically admitted that "all the petitioners were residing separately and doing their independent business and maintaining themselves.

Even prior to one and a half years of the death, the deceased and his wife were living separately, and all the claimant Nos. 2 to 4 were residing separately ," which itself shows that claimant Nos. 2 to 4 were neither residing with the deceased nor dependent on him.

Therefore, in my view, they are not entitled to claim compensation under the head of filial consortium, as they were neither reliant on the deceased nor residing with him or living in the company of the deceased.
But they were residing separately and maintaining themselves.

20. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajesh Vs. Rajbir Singh, (2013) 9 SCC 54, in paragraph No. 17 has considered and explained the meaning of the word "consortium" which thus reads as under :
"17....

In legal parlance, "consortium" is the right of the spouse to the company, care,
help, comfort, guidance, society, solace, affection and sexual relations with his or her mate.
That non-pecuniary head of damages has not been properly understood by our courts.
The loss of companionship, love, care and protection, etc., that the spouse is entitled to get has to be compensated appropriately.

The concept of non-pecuniary damage for loss of consortium is one of the major heads of award of compensation in other parts of the world, more particularly in the United States of America, Australia,
etc.
English courts have also recognised the right of a spouse to get compensation even during the period of temporary disablement.

By loss of consortium, the courts have made an attempt to compensate the loss of spouse's affection, comfort, solace,
companionship, society, assistance, protection, care and sexual relations during the future years.

Unlike the compensation awarded in other countries and other jurisdictions, since the legal heirs are otherwise adequately compensated for the pecuniary loss, it would not be proper to award a major amount under this head.

Hence, we are of the view that it would only be just and reasonable that the courts award at least rupees one lakh for loss of consortium."
21.

In Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others,
(2018) 18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex Court, in paragraphs 21, 21.1 to 21.3, interpreted "consortium"
and discussed who is entitled to get compensation under the head of loss of consortium.

In 21.2, the Hon'ble Apex Court explained the "parental consortium", wherein it is observed that "Parental consortium" is to be granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of "parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training"
22.

The three Judges Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs. Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur, (2021) 11 SCC 780, after considering the observations made in Nanu Ram (supra), has followed the explanation given therein.

23. As per Black's Law Dictionary, the meaning of 'consortium' is as under :

5 "consortium - 1.

sentences.text: The benefits that one person, esp. a spouse, is entitled to receive from another, including companionship, cooperation, affection, aid, financial support, and (between spouses) sexual relations.
Filial consortium - A child's society, affection, and companionship given to a parent.
Parental consortium.
A parent's society, affection, and companionship are given to a child.
Spousal consortium.
A spouse's society, affection, and companionship are given to the other spouse.
24. A bare perusal of paragraph 17 above, and the meaning of the word 'consortium' is defined and explained.

In legal parlance, "consortium" is the right of the spouse to the company, care, help,
comfort, guidance, society, solace, affection and sexual relations with his or her mate or which is a loss to his or her family.
25. Thus, it appears that there is no clarity with respect to the principles on which the compensation could be awarded on loss of parental consortium.

However, as observed in Nanu Ram and Satinder (supra), as well as the definition of the parental consortium given in Black's Law Dictionary, it is evident that " the parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of the parents for the loss of a "parental aid protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.".
26. While the Indian Constitution does not explicitly define a child, many Indian Laws, including the Juvenile Justice Act, define a child as someone under the age of 18 years.
Under the Juvenile Justice Act, under Section 2(12), a 'child' means "the person who has not completed 18 years of age".
In Black's Law Dictionary, the definition of 'child' means "a person under the age of majority ".
The above terminology of parental consortium primarily demonstrates that the parental consortium is to be granted to the " child upon the premature death of a parent".
It also indicates that a child does not include a major son or an independent earning son.
From the intent of the legislature or the definition of 'Parental consortium', it can be inferred that the major earning son is omitted.
In the case at hand, it is undisputed that claimants Nos. 2 to 4 are major, independent sons, and they are living separately from the deceased.
27. The evidence on record clearly indicates that the parents are residing separately.
The father was 82 years old, and the mother was also of advanced age.
Given their stage in life, it would be natural to expect that they would rely on their children for support and care.

Under both moral and social norms, as well as the broader principles underlying familial jurisprudence, adult children bear a corresponding obligation to provide for and attend to the needs of their ageing parents.
In such circumstances, it becomes a moral and filial obligation of the children to ensure the well-being and comfort of their elderly parents.
However, the fact that the parents are living apart suggests a lapse in this familial responsibility.

It raises concerns about the children's attentiveness to their parents'
needs in their twilight years.

Moreover, the fact that the parents are living apart is indicative of a Champabai Wd/O Jawaharlal ... vs Mr. Dinesh Purushottam Thakre And ... on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39219835/
6 failure on the part of the children to discharge their obligation, thereby reflecting a possible neglect of parental care and support expected under law and social standards.

sentences.text: 28. In the case at hand, it appears that applicants No. 2 to 4 are all major sons who were residing separately, doing their own independent business, and maintaining themselves .
They were neither living with him nor in his company or association.

Thus, it cannot be said that they were '
dependent' on the deceased or are entitled to get the compensation under the head of ' Parental consortium'.

Despite the said fact, it appears that the learned Tribunal awarded Rs. 44,000/- filial consortium (it should be under 'Parental consortium' ) to the petitioners No. 2 to 4 can be said to be more than sufficient.

29. The facts in Seema Rani's case, the sons had a low income and were largely dependent on the income of the deceased, and more particularly, they resided with the deceased jointly; however, in the case at hand, the facts differ as stated above.
It does not appear from the said judgment that the claimants therein were residing separately from the deceased.

Therefore, in my view, the observations made in the said judgment are of hardly any assistance to the claimants/appellants in support of their contention on the point of claiming the compensation under the head of consortium as well as dependency.

On the contrary, in view of the mandate laid down in the case of Vinish Jain (supra), the claimant Nos. 2 to 4 cannot be considered as dependent on the deceased, and therefore,
the deduction made by the learned Tribunal appears to be just and proper, and no interference is required in it.
30.

In Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Divya Girish Kapadiya, 2023 (3) T.A.C. 50 (Bom .),
the facts were that the deceased was 54 years old and all the claimants therein were dependent on him; therefore, the Court granted compensation under the head of 'Parental consortium'.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Divya Girish Kapadiya, 2023 (3) T.A.C. 50 (Bom .)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However,
as discussed above, the facts in the case at hand differ from those in Divya's case.
Therefore, the observations made therein do not apply to the case at hand and are hardly of assistance to the claimants in support of their contention.

31. Thus, the upshot of the above discussion is that the appellants/claimants failed to demonstrate that the impugned judgment is illegal and perverse to interfere in it in the appellate jurisdiction, or they are entitled to claim enhanced compensation under the head of dependency and 'parental consortium'.
On the contrary, no error or legal infirmity in the findings expressed by the learned Tribunal.
As such, the appeal being bereft of merit stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.

(ABHAY J. MANTRI, J.) Jayashree..
